note: Layout and accessibility behaviour is decided by SwiftUI at runtime on a device, so most of this matrix is a device checklist. Where the app makes the decision itself — reduced motion, the iPad split layout, the offline card state — it is covered by a test.

blocked.reason: Needs a device or simulator run; the size class decision belongs to SwiftUI.
blocked.expected_evidence: Every plan section is reachable in the compact tab layout with no clipped or unreachable control.

blocked.evidence_command: Open Spark.app, resize from the minimum width to full screen, and switch to menu-bar mode.
blocked.expected_evidence: No view collapses below its minimum content size and the menu-bar mode keeps status readable.

blocked.reason: Needs a device run at the accessibility text sizes.
blocked.evidence_command: In the simulator: Settings > Accessibility > Larger Text at AX5, then walk the dashboard.
blocked.expected_evidence: No label truncates and no control becomes unreachable at AX5.

blocked.reason: Needs VoiceOver, which is a system service.
blocked.evidence_command: Enable VoiceOver on the device and traverse onboarding and the dashboard.
blocked.expected_evidence: Every control has a label and value; the operation progress is announced.

blocked.reason: Needs the system Increase Contrast setting.
blocked.evidence_command: Enable Increase Contrast, then screenshot the dashboard in light and dark.
blocked.expected_evidence: Every text/background pair meets the contrast ratio the design system declares.

blocked.evidence_command: With a keyboard attached, traverse the app using Tab and arrow keys only.
blocked.expected_evidence: Focus order follows the visual order and every action is reachable without a pointer.

blocked.reason: Needs a paired device and a second administrator to revoke it mid-session.
blocked.evidence_command: With the app open on the dashboard, revoke that device from another: DELETE /api/v1/devices/{id} with a presence proof.
blocked.expected_evidence: The app's next request fails with 401 and the app returns to pairing rather than showing stale data.
